# Clue shapes

<!-- CLUE_SHAPES-START generated by tools/clue_shapes.py: do not edit -->

Every annotated clue's wordplay tree reduced to a skeleton (op tree, leaves abstracted to a type), over 556,489 clues in 57,366 puzzles: 21,558 distinct skeletons, folded into coarser groups below. Generated by `tools/clue_shapes.py` (`nice -n 19 python3 tools/clue_shapes.py`, about five minutes); the judgements come from `tools/data/clue_shape_verdicts.json`, which the tool never writes.

Leaf types: **V** verbatim clue words (and any fodder under an anagram, hidden or selection op), **F** folded (`gives` is part of the words, or the words part of `gives`: a link word, indicator or selection swallowed by the leaf), **A** one or two letters from other words (abbreviation, symbol), **S** synonym or other `gives`, **B** bare letters with no clue words, **U** unchecked leaf. `(a+b)` is a charade; `ana`, `ins` (container), `del`, `rev`, `hid`, `sound`, `spoon`, `sub`, `cyc`, `pal`, `cdef` (cryptic definition), `rebus` (a picture of letters), `comp` (composite anagram), `reverse` (reverse clue), `first last mid outer alt reg nth` (letter selection) name the other ops; `?` after an op name means its node is unchecked. Definition key: `2d` is the number of definitions, then where each sits (S start, E end, W whole clue, M middle); `&lit` when andLit is set.

## Three ways to group the shapes

The skeleton (tier 3) keeps charade order and arity and every leaf type, so there are thousands. Two coarser groupings sit above it; each is computed from the skeleton, so the verdicts still key on tier 3, and the full skeleton tables further down stay as the place to look for errors.

- **Tier 1, mechanism set**: which non-charade ops the clue uses, in any number and nesting. The letter selections (`first last mid outer alt reg nth`) count as one op, `select`; a clue with more than 3 different ops is one group; `charade only` is a clue with no other op.
- **Tier 2, mechanism tree**: the op nesting with each leaf (any type) written `x`, siblings sorted and deduplicated so order and arity vanish, a charade that is only leaves written `x`, and a charade of ops written `+[...]` at the top of the tree (a charade that merely builds one operand of an op is dropped). `ins(ana(x),x)` (an anagram put inside a word) and `ana(ins(x))` (an anagram of a container) stay distinct. A tree of more than 3 op nodes is one group, `4+ ops`. Definition placement is dropped.
- **Tier 3, skeleton**: the exact skeleton, as in the tables further down.

| tier | groups | cover 50% | cover 90% | cover 99% | groups with one clue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 mechanism set | 114 | 4 | 13 | 30 | 14 |
| 2 mechanism tree | 596 | 4 | 24 | 96 | 167 |
| 3 skeleton | 21,558 | 16 | 998 | 15994 | 13,062 |

## Skeletons with no verdict yet

None: every skeleton of at least 150 clues has a verdict.

## Still being fixed

32,729 clues (5.88%) have a skeleton judged other than ok, in 13 groups, ranked by clues. These are errors in the repair queue (`tools/data/shape_reannotate.json`), not a standing statistic; the list shrinks to None as the queue drains. `right` is the shape the clue should have.

### 1. unchecked node (parse not verified): 23,868 clues (4.29%), unverified

- why: an op or leaf the validator could not rebuild step by step; its letters are taken as filed, so nothing says the shape is real (spoonerisms, cyclings, substitutions, reversals of part of a word and indirect anagrams are most of them)
- right: re-annotate so every step is checked; none can be added now (the ratchet)
- 4373 skeletons; commonest `del?(S)` (980)
  - `azed-1736#28d` Factions second to last in ramble (JUNTA) = `del<second to last>([ramble]JAUNT)`
  - `canberra-720610#25d` Part of Kaspar's grand child's steering apparatus (HELM) = `del<Part of>([Kaspar's grand child]WILHELMINE)`
  - `cryptic-21781#2d` Work-to-rule neither starting nor finishing in the capital (OSLO) = `del<neither starting nor finishing>([Work-to-rule]GOSLOW)`

### 2. anagram wrapped around a container: 1,968 clues (0.35%), mislabelled

- why: the anagram is stored outside the container, as the last step, but the clues work the other way: a synonym or word is the container and an anagram of clue words goes inside it (FLYPITCH: LYP, an anagram of 'ply', inside FITCH, 'fur'; SECRETARIATE: CRETA, an anagram of 'crate', inside SERIATE). Almost all are unchecked, so nothing refused the wrong nesting
- right: ins(outer, ana(V)): the anagram is the container's inner arm
- 155 skeletons; commonest `ana?(ins(S,V))` (415)
  - `azed-1744#1a` Illegal stall the crooked ply, hung about with fur (FLYPITCH) = `ana<crooked>(ins<hung about with>([fur]FITCH, [ply]))`
  - `canberra-860707#21a` Lady was taken in perhaps by cable (HAWSER) = `ana<perhaps>(ins<taken in>([Lady]HER, [was]))`
  - `cryptic-21684#26a` Where the flytrap was you can see little bits mangled inside (WEBSITE) = `ana<mangled>(ins<inside>([little]WEE, [bits]))`

### 3. indirect anagram (fodder is a synonym): 1,731 clues (0.31%), rare

- why: the anagram's fodder is another word's synonym, which only Azed, Mephisto and a few toughies expect solvers to find; in daily puzzles it is an error unless the clue flags it, and in many of these the leaf has simply respelled the printed words
- right: ana(V) over the printed words when the leaf only dropped a link word or respelled; a deliberate indirect anagram stays
- 125 skeletons; commonest `ana(S)` (1,023)
  - `azed-1754#23a` A couple of boundaries dismantled over-fancy stuff (FROUFROU) = `ana<dismantled>([A couple of boundaries]FOURFOUR)`
  - `azed-2626#27a` Business, one that's died, parts reallocated (ERGON) = `ana<parts reallocated>([one that's died]GONER)`
  - `azed-2639#26d` Couple finally changing places in sign of approval embrace (CLASP) = `ana<Couple finally changing places>([sign of approval]CLAPS)`

### 4. same letter selection repeated word by word: 1,629 clues (0.29%), redundant

- why: an acrostic (heads of each word, tails, middles) built as one op per word inside a charade, usually with the indicator on the first op only, where the clue means one pick across a phrase
- right: one first/last/mid/outer/nth op over a single multi-word leaf
- 329 skeletons; commonest `(mid(V)+mid(V)+mid(V))` (154)
  - `azed-1976#24a` Product of separation revealing couples in hell (dual item) (ELUATE) = `(mid<couples in>([hell]) + mid([dual]) + mid([item]))`
  - `book-26052#22a` Obscure couples regularly found in county museum events (UNSEEN) = `(mid<couples regularly found in>([county]) + mid([museum]) + mid([events]))`
  - `cryptic-22478#20d` Contents of City Hall vice * (ITALIC) = `(mid<Contents of>([City]) + mid([Hall]) + mid([vice]))`

### 5. four or more mechanisms in one clue: 950 clues (0.17%), rare

- why: four non-charade ops (nested containers with deletions and reversals, long acrostics) is more than a solver can unpick from a clue; real setters stop at two, occasionally three; the commonest are acrostics, double containers around acrostics, and one deletion written letter by letter, del(del(del(..))), that is really one op (an op nested four deep always lands here, so there is no separate depth rule)
- right: fewer ops: merge repeated selections, flatten containers, or check the parse
- 741 skeletons; commonest `ins(ins(S,first(V)),first(V))` (25)
  - `cryptic-22063#26a` Silence enshrouds upper and lower prison camps (GULAG) = `ins<enshrouds>(ins([Silence]GAG, first<upper and lower>([upper])), first([lower]))`
  - `cyclops-425#26a` Faction of eventual Labour leaders into mugging (THELEFT) = `ins<into>(ins([mugging]THEFT, first<leaders>([eventual])), first([Labour]))`
  - `everyman-4017#16d` Chef's instructions: pieces of endive and chicory … filling … ready to eat (RECIPE) = `ins<filling>(ins([ready to eat]RIPE, first<pieces of>([chicory])), first([endive]))`

### 6. wordplay that is one synonym leaf: 752 clues (0.14%), mislabelled

- why: a tree of a single leaf is no wordplay at all: it restates the answer as one 'synonym' of the clue words, or is a cross-reference ('See 1')
- right: a cryptic definition, a double definition, or a real parse; a cross-reference belongs to the linked group
- 4 skeletons; commonest `S` (724)
  - `azed-1734#33a` What is after c for cyanite?! (DISTHENE) = `[What is after c]DISTHENE`
  - `book-16004#24a` Assign no Gospels? (ALLOT) = `[no Gospels]ALLOT`
  - `canberra-670923#17d` All points to a religious sect (ESSENES) = `[All points]ESSENES`

### 7. letter selection from a synonym: 659 clues (0.12%), rare

- why: an initial, ending or middle taken from a synonym rather than from the clue's own words is a hard Azed/Mephisto device; in the daily papers these are almost all a fodder leaf that swallowed the indicator or a link word ('[Cameron's first]CAMERONFIRST')
- right: sel(V) over exactly the fodder words; the indicator belongs on the op
- 164 skeletons; commonest `mid(S)` (305)
  - `azed-1807#11d` Producer topped and tailed Spenserian tale (REEDE) = `mid<topped and tailed>([Producer]BREEDER)`
  - `book-11041#23a` Victim of Cyclops is heartily disparaging of other cultures (ACIS) = `mid<heartily>([disparaging of other cultures]RACIST)`
  - `cryptic-22191#21d` Take away top and bottom drawers for £1? (NICKER) = `mid<Take away top and bottom>([drawers]KNICKERS)`

### 8. answer letters with no clue words in a charade: 525 clues (0.09%), mislabelled

- why: a charade piece (or fodder piece) made of letters no clue word supplies: an unexplained gap in the parse, not a mechanism
- right: the leaf for the clue word that supplies them (an abbreviation or a selection)
- 323 skeletons; commonest `(B+S)` (38)
  - `azed-2209#15d` One uttering shrill cry (animal by the sound of it?) (CREECHER) = `(S + [animal by the sound of it]CREECHER)`
  - `cryptic-22231#22a` Don't take away food for plant hormone (ZEATIN) = `(Z + [Don't take away food]EATIN)`
  - `genius-1#10a` Busy bird (ATIT) = `(A + [bird]TIT)`

### 9. reversal and anagram stacked: 399 clues (0.07%), redundant

- why: an anagram's output order is free, so reversing it (or anagramming a reversal) adds nothing; in these clues the reverse indicator really sits on a different piece, or the intermediate word is an invented string
- right: one anagram over the fodder, with the reversal on its own sibling piece if there is one
- 157 skeletons; commonest `(rev(S)+rev(ana(V)))` (29)
  - `azed-2281#10a` Teacher having turned sour I exercised what causes a smile? (RISORIUS) = `(rev<having turned>([Teacher]SIR) + rev(ana<exercised>([sour I])))`
  - `canberra-900814#14a` Annoy over number let out (NETTLE) = `(rev<over>([number]TEN) + rev(ana<out>([let])))`
  - `cryptic-22070#18d` Manage to rise above tear about having to tell a tale (NARRATE) = `(rev<rise>([Manage]RAN) + rev(ana<about>([tear])))`

### 10. letter selection over another selection or op: 74 clues (0.01%), implausible

- why: a pick made from the result of another operation (first of the outer letters, first of the middle); a setter writes one selection, so this is a two-step the clue does not print, or a leaf that swallowed an indicator
- right: one selection op over the fodder words, or the picks as separate pieces of a charade
- 39 skeletons; commonest `first?(outer(V))` (8)
  - `cryptic-26842#5d` * It flies to the boundaries of Ethiopia (ELAL) = `first<the boundaries of>(outer([Ethiopia]))`
  - `ftcryptic-16523#26d` Instrument from borders of Zaire — twice (ZEZE) = `first<borders of>(outer<twice>([Zaire]))`
  - `independent-12171#11a` Both sides of strategy for Alexander (SANDY) = `first<Both sides of>(outer([strategy]))`

### 11. anagram of a charade of verbatim words: 66 clues (0.01%), redundant

- why: the fodder is cut into word-by-word leaves joined by an unindicated charade, which says nothing a single multi-word fodder leaf does not; the charade is not a mechanism here, it is the fodder written in pieces
- right: ana(V): one leaf holding all the fodder words
- 8 skeletons; commonest `ana?((V+V))` (37)
  - `azed-2062#10d` Nigella gargled wildly on broadcast day (RAGGEDLADY) = `ana<wildly><broadcast>(([gargled] + [day]))`
  - `canberra-751218#2d` Verbal approval of a brace of cooked hare! (HEARHEAR) = `ana<cooked>(([hare] + [hare])<a brace of>)`
  - `cryptic-21911#18d` Different for rich? That's appalling! (HORRIFIC) = `ana<Different>(([for] + [rich]))`

### 12. palindrome with its definition or indicator stored as leaves: 57 clues (0.01%), mislabelled

- why: the palindrome op wraps unchecked leaves that are the definition and the indicator rather than letters
- right: pal<indicator>([fodder]) or pal() over the answer alone
- 2 skeletons; commonest `pal(U)` (53)
  - `canberra-671216#10a` The principle's the same, anyway (TENET) = `pal<the same, anyway>([principle])`
  - `cryptic-22397#11a` Something done both ways (DEED) = `pal<both ways>([Something done])`
  - `everyman-3270#8d` Act, one way or the other (DEED) = `pal<one way or the other>([one way or the other])`

### 13. charade directly inside a charade: 51 clues (0.01%), redundant

- why: a charade is associative, so a bracketed charade inside a charade changes nothing; most carry a trailing unchecked leaf of leftover words
- right: one flat charade (or an indicator on the whole charade)
- 43 skeletons; commonest `((S+cyc(S)))` (3)
  - `indysunday-1559#29a` Series on musical group first to last getting to act unrestrainedly (RUNRIOT) = `(([Series]RUN + cyc<first to last>([musical group]TRIO)))<on>`
  - `toughie-3266#20d` Peak of success when cycling, with belief to come first (ZENITH) = `(([belief]ZEN + cyc<cycling>([success]HIT)))<to come first>`

Notes on the commonest:

- `DD`: a double definition: two definitions, no wordplay, the one family with no tree
- `ana(V)`: the plain anagram of clue words
- `(S+S)`: the plain charade of two synonyms
- `del(S,B)`: the removed letters are stored bare (no clue words), as a head, tail or inner deletion of a few letters; legitimate, but a positional deletion (first/last letter) carries its meaning only in the indicator
- `ins(ins(S,A),A)`: one outer word with two inserts but, in nearly every clue, an indicator on the outer container only: the inner container is unindicated, so the tree says 'inside' twice for one phrase; a single container with a charade as its inner arm is the other way to write it
